data.title: Nvidia (NVDA) Stock Price Defies Q3 Earnings Strength As Margin Questions Linger
data.description:
NVIDIA came into this Q3 2027 print with a heavy reputation as the engine of artificial intelligence, yet the stock closed down 2.9% to US$150.96 the first full day after results. That move jars with the headline numbers. Quarterly revenue reached US$115.8b and basic earnings per share hit US$2.71, while trailing net profit margins sat at a very high 62.5%. The expectation gap is clear. Price suggested fatigue, while the financial update pointed to a business still printing unusually rich profits for a chip designer.

Love NVIDIA’s huge profits but uneasy about a market that shrugs at 62.5% margins and triple digit quarterly revenue in billions? Benchmark those instincts against our 30 resilient stocks with low risk scores.

Q3 2027 Earnings Summary

  • Revenue (Q3 2027 vs Q3 2026): US$115.8b vs. US$57.0b (very large increase in quarterly sales)
  • Net Income (Excl. Extra Items, Q3 2027 vs Q3 2026): US$65.3b vs. US$31.9b (very large increase in quarterly profit)
  • Basic EPS (Q3 2027 vs Q3 2026): US$2.71 vs. US$1.31 (roughly doubled earnings per share)
  • Trailing Net Profit Margin (Last 12 Months vs Prior Year): 62.5% vs. 53.0% (margin higher year on year, with a large non cash component in earnings)

Prefer clean visual charts over slogging through dense earnings releases and raw figures? Get a full visual read on NVIDIA with a clear view of its valuation in the company report for NVIDIA.

NVIDIA’s AI Factory Ambition Meets Hard Numbers

The bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St argues that NVIDIA can turn its expanded platform into multi year compounding power.

"The main thing that has to go right is that NVIDIA continues to scale its full stack AI factory platform with supply constrained demand across hyperscalers and ACIE customers, while managing memory cost pressures and the loss of China data center compute revenue."

Q3 goes a long way toward that objective. Data center revenue of about US$108b, alongside roughly US$20b from Vera Rubin’s first production quarter, indicates broad take up of full systems rather than just chips. ACI&E near US$47b shows the non hyperscaler engine is already material, even as China data center sales are effectively excluded from guidance.

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the higher Fair Value this Narrative argues for.

NVIDIA: Bear Fears On Margin Durability Get A Real Test

The bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St argues that richer AI factory systems may not fully protect profitability once component costs bite.

"While NVIDIA now positions itself as a full AI factory platform provider with rising revenue opportunity per gigawatt of deployed capacity, the company’s guidance that gross margins bottom near 71 to 72% and only stabilize a bit higher by fiscal 2028 shows that richer system content may not fully offset component inflation and supply chain burden, which could reduce the operating leverage implied in many long term earnings models."

Q3 reported gross margins around 74.8 to 74.9% and management still points to a Q4 trough at 71 to 72%, so the compression the quote worries about is now explicitly in the outlook. At the same time, trailing net margin at 62.5% remains very high and Q4 revenue is guided up to about US$130b, which means NVIDIA is absorbing higher memory and financing costs without a collapse in earnings power. The bearish view is not invalidated, but the hit so far looks controlled rather than severe.

data.title: Revenue Beat: AFFIN Bank Berhad Exceeded Revenue Forecasts By 10% And Analysts Are Updating Their Estimates
data.description:
As you might know, AFFIN Bank Berhad (KLSE:AFFIN) just kicked off its latest third-quarter results with some very strong numbers. It was a positive result, with revenues and statutory earnings per share (EPS) both performing well. Revenues were 10% higher than the analysts had forecast, at RM691m, while EPS of RM0.043 beat analyst models by 2.8%. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We've gathered the most recent statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their earnings models, following these results.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from AFFIN Bank Berhad's nine analysts is for revenues of RM2.80b in 2027. This reflects a decent 15% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to ascend 20% to RM0.23. Before this earnings report, the analysts had been forecasting revenues of RM2.82b and earnings per share (EPS) of RM0.24 in 2027. The analysts seem to have become a little more negative on the business after the latest results, given the minor downgrade to their earnings per share numbers for next year.

View our latest analysis for AFFIN Bank Berhad

The average price target fell 9.3% to RM2.16, with reduced earnings forecasts clearly tied to a lower valuation estimate. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. There are some variant perceptions on AFFIN Bank Berhad, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at RM2.50 and the most bearish at RM1.92 per share. This is a very narrow spread of estimates, implying either that AFFIN Bank Berhad is an easy company to value, or - more likely - the analysts are relying heavily on some key assumptions.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. We can infer from the latest estimates that forecasts expect a continuation of AFFIN Bank Berhad'shistorical trends, as the 12% annualised revenue growth to the end of 2027 is roughly in line with the 10% annual growth over the past five years. Compare this with the broader industry, which analyst estimates (in aggregate) suggest will see revenues grow 6.2% annually. So although AFFIN Bank Berhad is expected to maintain its revenue growth rate, it's definitely expected to grow faster than the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest concern is that the analysts reduced their earnings per share estimates, suggesting business headwinds could lay ahead for AFFIN Bank Berhad. Fortunately, they also reconfirmed their revenue numbers, suggesting that it's tracking in line with expectations. Additionally, our data suggests that revenue is expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target fell measurably, with the analysts seemingly not reassured by the latest results, leading to a lower estimate of AFFIN Bank Berhad's future valuation.

Following on from that line of thought, we think that the long-term prospects of the business are much more relevant than next year's earnings. We have forecasts for AFFIN Bank Berhad going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here.

A company's cash runway is the amount of time it would take to burn through its cash reserves at its current cash burn rate.
